5: There are people who do not care for hunters, and they may not be wholly in the wrong.
6: Is it perhaps because lords do not themselves pursue game,
7: that they will eat and kill with their own hands, and thus act as butchers?
8: Or may that lesser sympathy also arise from this—that gentlemen and hunters love
9: to talk of their hunting exploits, always and ever, and all too often?
10: I shall not be persuaded from that opinion by any late objection.
11: It is now twenty years since I committed the first crime.
14: And to punish me for it, I shall commit the proven second crime: I shall tell you my hunting adventures.
16: May this story, this truthful and honest story, frighten my fellow men from it for ever—
17: with an Alpine rucksack on the back, with a cartridge pouch at the waist,
18: with the rifle under the arm, behind the tail of a dog trailing across the field!
19: But I do not count on it, I must confess!
